_readme: Hand-added code in the three files scripts/extract-mockup.mjs OWNS (markup.html, style.css, main.js) that its mockup does not have. This registry is the RECORD half of gh#212, not the refusal half: what stops data loss is the extractor refusing to overwrite any file it already ships whose bytes would change, whether or not anybody wrote it down here. What this file adds is why a divergence is deliberate and who owns it (owner ruling 2026-09-05), and one power the file-level refusal does not have — a fragment listed here cannot be released by --force at all, only by editing this file, so releasing it is a reviewed diff. scripts/mockup-divergence-check.mjs also reds if a recorded fragment has already gone from the shipped tree. The mockups stay the original design record and are never edited to match. deliberate=false records a divergence nobody has ruled on yet and is NOT enforced. An entry may instead set absent=true, owner ruling 2026-09-08 (gh#220): its fragment must NOT appear in the shipped file, and the check reds when a re-extraction puts it back. That kind exists because a decision whose content is that something is not here has no fragment to assert as present, so it could not be recorded at all. It inherits the escape-hatch rule word for word -- --force releases an absence no more than it releases a presence, and the extractor refuses before it writes either way. What no run can check is the other half: the fragment is asserted absent from what ships, in this repo, while the mockup it would come back from lives outside version control, so nothing here proves the forbidden text is still at the source. Enumerate the full drift, one line per mockup/route pair, with: node scripts/mockup-divergence-check.mjs --enumerate. FINDING, owner ruling 2026-09-08 (gh#222): every one of the 11 paired routes carries drift, so the discriminator is not whether a route drifted but whether the drift is recorded here -- and exactly two routes have NOTHING recorded, short-stick (all three files would be overwritten) and pinocchio-luck (markup.html and main.js). Nobody has ruled on either, so no entry can be written: the schema needs a fragment per entry and which bytes are hand-edits is exactly what is unknown. The owner ruled these two are recorded as a finding and NOT re-extracted. Re-extraction is already refused by the file-level pre-write seam, which does not need this registry; the live hazard is somebody reaching for --force <owner> and reading the absence of entries here as 'nothing to lose'. For those two routes it means the opposite. Re-check with --enumerate before trusting this sentence's route list -- it is dated, and a third route could join it.

markup.html.why: the shared play-screen-fit walk finds a route's play surface by #app / #app-container / #appRoot; the mockup's root carries no id, and a root the walk cannot find is a route it cannot measure at all
the shared player screen's root (ADR-0071), holding the mockup's own title and intro above it; the mockup's setup screen it replaced is recorded absent below
the mockup's own count stepper; the count belongs to the shared player screen (ADR-0071), and a re-extraction that put it back would give this route two count controls
the mockup's own name rows; names belong to the shared player screen and the shared roster (ADR-0071)
the mockup ships its setup screen active; the player screen is the first screen now, and an active setup would show over it with no players chosen

main.js.why: the owner reported turning was too slow and chose 2.8 half-widths per second over the mockup's 1.8, which halves a full-road crossing from 1.11s to 0.71s. A feel-tuned scalar like CENTRIFUGAL beside it, not derived, so the mockup will never agree with it. drift-rules.test.mjs also pins the behaviour, but only this entry survives a --force: the file layer can be forced past for one run and the fragment layer cannot

the reduced-motion dt factor, moved into the RULES table from a literal in the frame loop so drift-rules.test.mjs can red on a wrong value at all. This is the constant half of a pair: on its own it can sit in the table unused

the connector, and the half no test can see: the frame loop is outside the @logic-start block drift-rules.test.mjs slices. A re-extraction that keeps REDUCED_DT in the table and restores a literal here leaves the constant dead with every assertion still green, which is why the call site is recorded and not only the constant
the ghost-tap gate every reveal path on this route runs through; the mockup has no arm gate at all
the shared player screen mount, its startWithPlayers entry and the putAwayRound that ends a round from it (ADR-0071); the mockup builds its own setup instead
the mockup's own name-row builder; a re-extraction that put it back would rebuild a setup the shared screen replaced
show() is the one seam every screen change passes through, so this is every reveal path the route's own screens have; src/play/bangkok-drift/arm-reveal-paths.test.mjs drives all four
the button is empty in markup, so it carries a generic accessible name from src/play/_aria-labels.json; this keeps that name equal to the text the player can read once the round fills it
a play route never blanks the page: the mockup calls getContext unguarded at module top level, which aborts the whole module on a device out of 2D contexts

style.css.why: the wrapper carries no viewport floor on purpose -- body already has one plus a padding-bottom, so a second floor here made the document taller than the screen and the play screen scrolled with nothing to see. The mockup sets both floors on .app-wrapper, so a re-extraction restores them. The leading align-items line is part of the fragment as a DISAMBIGUATOR, not as forbidden content: the two min-height declarations on their own also appear on body, where they are correct, and trimming this fragment to them would red the file permanently.

the escape helper the mockup has no equivalent of — it interpolates a seat label into innerHTML raw. Player names are a set this site does not own (ADR-0026), so the guard sits where the markup is AUTHORED, and this declaration is that place; a re-extraction restores the raw sink and only name-escaping.test.mjs goes red, after the bytes are gone

the call site, recorded separately from the helper above because the two fail apart: a helper nothing calls is an escape sink in name only, and this is the route's one markup-by-string hole that carries a player-typed name

the camera centres the board in the space the HUD leaves free instead of in the whole viewport. The mockup has no site HUD, so its camera centres on the viewport and the turn banner ends up sitting on the board's top edge — measured at 1440x900, the board's topmost rendered row was 119 on a five-by-five board and 104 on a nine-by-nine against a banner bottom of 123, so the bigger the roster the worse it is. Recorded rather than left to the file-level refusal because this is a behaviour decision with a reason, and because the fix cannot live in overrides.css: #gameCanvas is the full-viewport backdrop, so offsetting it exposes bare page background

the bias itself, recorded apart from the helper above because the two fail apart: the helper alone measures bands nothing reads, and this line alone reads a cache that is still at its {top: 0, bottom: 0} initialiser, which is a zero bias rather than a crash. That silence is exactly why all three lines are pinned separately

the CONNECTOR, and the one an adversarial review caught missing. The helper and the bias line above are both silent halves: a re-extraction that kept them and dropped the call that refreshes the cache would leave two recorded fragments present, this gate green, and the bias permanently zero — the board back under the banner with nothing red anywhere. That is the failure class gh#212 was filed on. Pinned on the counter name rather than the whole statement so changing the 30-frame interval does not red this entry for no reason

the engine's own stepper wiring and the DOM writes in its count setter; the stepper's nodes left markup.html with ADR-0071, and a re-extraction that put the lookups back would throw on the missing node before the rest of the engine binds
